title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: Your assistant's loop has just run a tool and is about to call the model a second time in the same request. How does the model know what happened in the first call?

options.text: The program sends the earlier messages again as part of the input
The model keeps a private memory of its earlier call until it ends
The model looks up its earlier call in the provider's saved logs
The tool sends its result straight into the model's stored memory

items.stem: In one request, the system prompt and tool descriptions take 800 tokens and the student's question takes 200. The model's first call outputs a 30-token tool request, the tool returns a 600-token result, and a second call writes the final answer. Counting only input tokens, how many tokens are sent to the model across the two calls?
A student finishes bandsaw training today and comes back next month. Which design lets the assistant know about the training then?

options.text: A model with a window big enough to hold today's whole chat
A short saved record, loaded into the context at session start
A system prompt that tells the model to remember each student
A chat history kept inside the model after the session closes

items.stem: Your teammate suggests pasting all twelve machine manuals into the system prompt of every request. Give one reason, in a sentence or two, why retrieving a few relevant chunks is better.
A student's session ends. Which of these is gone when the next session starts, unless your program saved it somewhere else?

options.text: The manuals stored in the search index
The booking records kept in the calendar system
The tool results held in that session's messages list
The notes file the program wrote to disk
